n: The first revelation in Kirtland, Ohio, February 4, 1831. The Lord delights to bless those who hear him with the greatest blessings — and warns professed believers who don’t listen.
The elders are to assemble and agree on God’s word.
By the prayer of faith they will receive God’s law to govern the Church. This promise was fulfilled days later in D&C 42, the “law of the Church.”
Christ will be their ruler at his coming, and he will see that his law is kept.

f.w: I will be your ruler when I come

n: A true disciple both receives and does the law; one who claims to receive it but doesn’t live it is not a disciple.

f.w: He that receiveth my law and doeth it, the same is my disciple

n: Sacred things should not be given to the unworthy — Jesus’ teaching about not casting pearls before swine.

f.w: the pearls to be cast before swine

n: Joseph should have a house built where he can live and continue translating the Bible.

f.w: a house built, in which to live and translate
f.g: Joseph and Emma lived for a time on Isaac Morley’s farm in Kirtland.

n: Sidney Rigdon may live as he sees fit, as long as he keeps the commandments.
Edward Partridge is called, by vote of the Church, as bishop — leaving his business to work full time for the Church. He became the first bishop of this dispensation.

f.g: Greek episkopos, “overseer”; a bishop cares for the poor and manages Church property.

n: He will handle all assignments under the laws God is about to reveal.
Edward is called because his heart is pure — like Nathanael, whom Jesus described as an Israelite without guile.

f.w: Nathanael of old, in whom there is no guile

n: These words are pure; how the Saints treat them will be answered at the judgment.
